description:
Origin: L2 blind-spot from the SCD2 adversarial audit (_project/blind-spots/2026-07-11-152233-remediation-verified-by-claim-not-evidence.md). Three review passes and a status:Completed TODO (scd2-validation-soundness-hardening) accepted the claim 'each op already backstops the existence side with a positive companion check' without checking it per op. It was true for 2 of the 3 SCD2 ops and FALSE for merge_scd_type2_no_change (zero positive assertions), which the audit's N2 finding later caught. The gap: remediation verification was done at the level of the *claim* rather than the *evidence* - a one-line per-op query would have caught it. Lesson (framework-gap, not instance defect): a collective claim ('each X has property P') is only as strong as its weakest instance, but a reviewer reading the claim text inherits the author's framing and checks the aggregate. Any review closing on a 'for each / collectively' premise must re-derive it instance-by-instance from the source of truth, preferring a mechanical enumeration (one query/grep per member) over rereading the claim.

Extend this existing process item using session 01a07292: the #2051 query-set fix passed focused tests while a partial fixture emptied the downstream read model. Publication receipt/journal/executor fixes also recurred across branches. Require per-instance evidence plus a bounded producer-to-persistence-to-consumer trace for each accepted defect class. Do not equate a high test count, static wording check, or zero current threads with an integrated outcome.

preserves.behavior: Blind-spot capture stays a valid separate mechanism; this registers the actionable process follow-up per the user directive to track all follow-ups as TODOs.
Leave unrelated completed tracker evidence untouched; new defects need explicit owned work rather than a blanket completion claim.
No automatic acceptance of review claims; no forcing a rebuttal quota; no generic framework extraction.
